record.paper_title: Basic kinetic wealth-exchange models: common features and open problems
record.context_brief: Stationary Gamma distribution in kinetic wealth-exchange models
record.original_question: For basic homogeneous kinetic wealth-exchange models involving stochastic pairwise wealth exchanges between agents, including the Angle A1/A2, Bennati B, Chakraborti-Chakrabarti C, and Dragulescu-Yakovenko D models, can one derive a general stationary solution for the equilibrium wealth distribution that identifies when a Gamma distribution is the true stationary distribution and explains the microscopic mechanism by which that Gamma form emerges, rather than relying on model-by-model fitting formulas?

evidence.quote: The close analogies among the various models are evident, however the existence of a general solution has not been demonstrated, see e.g. Refs. [23, 41].
However, a general demonstration that the Γ-distribution is the stationary solution of KWEMs and an understanding of how it arises is still missing

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a closed economy with N agents, where agent i holds wealth x_i ≥ 0 and the total wealth Σ x_i is conserved. Time evolves through stochastic binary collisions: at each step, an unordered pair (i,j) is chosen uniformly at random and their wealths (x_i, x_j) are updated to (x_i', x_j') = (x_i + x_j)(ξ, 1-ξ) (or a closely related rule), where ξ ∈ [0,1] is drawn from a model-specific distribution. Four specific update rules are considered:

(A1) "Angle 1": ξ chosen uniformly in [0,1].
(A2) "Angle 2": x_i' = x_i cos^2 θ + x_j sin^2 θ, x_j' = x_i sin^2 θ + x_j cos^2 θ, with θ uniform on [0, 2π).
(B) "Bennati": with probability 1/2 each, one agent gives a fixed fraction of its wealth to the other.
(C) "Chakraborti–Chakrabarti": x_i' = λ x_i + (1-λ)[ε(x_i+x_j)], x_j' = λ x_j + (1-λ)[(1-ε)(x_i+x_j)], where λ ∈ [0,1) is a fixed "saving propensity" and ε is uniform on [0,1].
(D) "Dragulescu–Yakovenko": x_i' = ε(x_i+x_j), x_j' = (1-ε)(x_i+x_j), with ε uniform on [0,1].

Empirically, the equilibrium one-agent wealth distribution f(x) in each of these models is well-fitted by a Gamma density
   f(x) = (1/Γ(n)) (n/⟨x⟩)^n x^{n-1} exp(-n x/⟨x⟩),
where the shape parameter n depends on the model (e.g. n = 1 for D, n is a function of λ for C).

Problem. Provide a unified derivation, applicable to the entire class of homogeneous pairwise wealth-exchange models above, that:
(i) gives the equilibrium one-agent marginal distribution as the explicit stationary solution of the underlying master/Boltzmann-type equation for the wealth distribution, and
(ii) characterizes precisely which exchange rules in this family yield an exact Gamma stationary distribution (as opposed to merely a Gamma-shaped approximation), identifying the microscopic mechanism—such as a symmetry, conservation law, or maximum-entropy principle—responsible for the emergence of the Gamma form.
artifact.status_search_result: For specific kinetic exchange rules (notably the Immediate Exchange Model and its Beta-distributed generalization) it has been rigorously shown using stochastic duality and SU(1,1) symmetry that the invariant measure is a product of Gamma distributions. Other works (e.g., "Wealth distribution: To be or not to be a Gamma?", 2010) have argued that for several basic KWEMs the Gamma form is only an approximation, not exact. A fully general unified derivation covering all of the A1, A2, B, C, D models simultaneously, with a single microscopic mechanism explaining the Gamma form, does not appear in the literature; only model-specific or sub-class results are available.

status_evidence.title: Duality and Stationary Distributions of the Immediate Exchange Model
status_evidence.snippet: Using duality and an underlying SU(1,1) symmetry, the invariant measure of the generalized Immediate Exchange Model is shown to be a product of Gamma distributions.
status_evidence.claim: For a specific generalization of KWEMs, the Gamma stationary distribution has been rigorously derived.

status_evidence.title: Wealth distribution: To be or not to be a Gamma?
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates whether the equilibrium wealth distribution in basic KWEMs is truly a Gamma distribution, finding it is only approximately Gamma for several models.
status_evidence.claim: For several basic KWEMs, the Gamma form is only approximate, indicating no universal exact result.
